subject: Audit-friendly data retention options & next steps
messages:
From: Bethany Cole <bethany.cole@finvista.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood-inference.com
Cc: Alex Torres <atorres@finvista.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up from today — privacy checklist and pilot ask

Hi Markus,

Thanks for walking us through Redwood's serving options today — good conversation. Per our call, I wanted to summarize our privacy/data handling asks and propose next steps so we can align internally at FinVista. High level: FinVista runs regulated financial workflows and we need tight controls around PII and logs.

Key asks from our legal/security team: 
- Zero-persistence mode for prompt content when feasible (we still need embeddings/outputs retained in specific downstream systems but want core prompt logs not persisted).
- Short diagnostic logs only (if required) — ideally 3-7 days, fully redact PII.
- Data residency: primary serving in us-west, with audit trail showing where inference ran.
- Evidence: SOC 2 summary + list of what logs exist and retention windows.

I've attached a one-page checklist and our redlines (PDF). Can Redwood do a pilot where:
1) We route a low-volume subset of traffic into a 0-retention configuration for 4 weeks,
2) A parallel debug stream captures only redacted metadata for up to 7 days, and
3) Redwood provides SOC2 evidence + a statement of KV cache behavior for the pilot.

Next steps from our side: legal wants a short mutual action plan (timeline + deliverables). Can you propose one and confirm whether this requires Redwood Private/Dedicated or can run on Hosted API with configuration flags?

Appreciate it — Bethany

--
Bethany Cole
Head of Product Security, FinVista
bethany.cole@finvista.com
+1 415-555-0123

From: markus.klein@redwood-inference.com <markus.klein@redwood-inference.com>
To: Bethany Cole <bethany.cole@finvista.com>
Cc: Alex Torres <atorres@finvista.com>, neha_kapoor@redwood-inference.com, karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com
Date: 2026-08-30T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today — privacy checklist and pilot ask

Bethany —

Thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. Confirming receipt and answering the core questions below. Short version: we can run a scoped pilot on Hosted API in a special configuration (no message persistence + limited debug logs) — it does not strictly require Private/Dedicated unless you need exclusive hardware for compliance reasons.

Answers / clarifications:
- Zero-persistence mode: Redwood supports an "ephemeral request" flag that prevents storing prompt text in persistent logs or long-term analytics. For the pilot, we can enable this for a route so those prompts are not written to disk or analytics tables.
- Debug logs: We can route diagnostics to a short TTL store (configurable). Typical pilot windows: 3, 7, or 14 days. We can start at 7 days per your ask and reduce if that meets audit needs. All debug logs support PII redaction rules; we'll work with you on the list of fields to redact.
- KV cache behavior: KV caches (for speed) are ephemeral in-memory and not persisted to long-term storage in our Hosted deployment; however, to be fully explicit we will provide a written statement for the pilot showing that KV entries are not saved beyond the worker lifetime.
- Residency: We can pin the host region to us-west for routing; we'll provide traceability in our audit artifacts.
- Evidence: attaching our SOC2 executive summary (redacted). Security can provide more detailed evidence via our secure portal upon NDA.

Proposed mutual action plan (suggested):
1) Week 0 (this week): Sign pilot SOW + NDA addendum for evidence access (2 business days).
2) Week 1: Redwood configures a dedicated route with ephemeral flag + 7-day debug TTL; test harness and sample prompts exchanged.
3) Weeks 2-5: Pilot run (low-volume traffic, ~1k requests/day). Redwood provides weekly snapshot logs (redacted) and an interim compliance note.
4) Week 6: Review meeting to decide expansion or additional controls (longer retention, Private deployment).

At a high level, Hosted API with per-route config should suffice for the pilot. If FinVista needs an isolated environment or contractual data residency guarantees beyond per-route pinning (e.g., data physically isolated for audit), we can map to Redwood Dedicated or Private. I'll loop Neha and Karthik on the technical/evidence details below.

Next immediate ask from us: can you confirm the sample data set for the pilot and the list of PII fields you want redacted? Also if legal has DocuSign redlines we should review.

I'll wait for your confirmation and will get a draft pilot SOW over today.

Thanks,
Markus
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood-inference.com
+1 650-555-0890

From: neha_kapoor@redwood-inference.com <neha_kapoor@redwood-inference.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood-inference.com
Cc: Bethany Cole <bethany.cole@finvista.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com
Date: 2026-08-31T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today — privacy checklist and pilot ask

Bethany/Markus —

Quick technical follow-up from security to make sure the SOW is accurate and that audit artifacts will satisfy FinVista's reviewers. A few clarifications we need to lock down before we finalize the pilot SOW: 

1) "Ephemeral request" semantics: this prevents prompt text from being written to persistent storage and telemetry tables. However, for debugging we may capture a redacted copy in a secured short-TTL store. Please confirm whether your auditors require hashes (SHA256) of prompts retained for repro purposes — we can emit hashes (non-reversible) to the audit log if helpful.

2) KV cache: the in-memory cache is per-worker and cleared on worker recycle. We will supply a signed statement that no KV persistence is enabled for the pilot route. If FinVista needs deterministic guarantees for forensic review, Dedicated/Private with explicit configuration is recommended.

3) Access controls & audit logs: RBAC for the pilot will be limited to a small set of Redwood engineers and your nominated reviewers. We'll provide a time-stamped audit trail for configuration changes and access.

4) Redaction: we need your initial redaction rule set (fields/regex examples). We'll apply a two-stage redaction: automatic pattern-based redaction + optional manual scrub if required.

Attachments: I'm attaching (to this message) a short checklist of artifacts we can provide during the pilot (endpoint logs, config snapshots, access logs). We'll add the signed KV cache statement to the evidence bundle.

If this looks good, I can sign off on the pilot SOW language and we can move to DocuSign.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood-inference.com

From: Bethany Cole <bethany.cole@finvista.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood-inference.com
Cc: Alex Torres <atorres@finvista.com>, neha_kapoor@redwood-inference.com, karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com
Date: 2026-09-02T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today — privacy checklist and pilot ask

Markus / Neha —

Thanks, this is helpful. We want to proceed with the Hosted pilot as described and will avoid Dedicated unless the auditors push back. A few concrete answers from our side to accelerate the SOW: 

- Pilot dataset: we'll send a synthetic sample set (redacted) by EOD Monday.
- Redaction fields: primary_account_number, ssn, email, phone, and 
  - anything matching / \d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4} / or common card number patterns.
- Hashes: we do NOT want prompt text preserved even as hashes for the pilot; hashes may complicate our audit claims.
- Desired debug TTL: 7 days to start.

Please prepare:
- Draft SOW with the mutual action plan you outlined,
- Signed KV cache non-persistence statement, and
- DocuSign-ready version of the one-page pilot SOW + NDA addendum (we attached redlines in the earlier PDF).

Alex and I will review the SOW internally and aim to return a signed DocuSign within 48 hours.

Best,
Bethany

--
Bethany Cole
Head of Product Security, FinVista
